{"id":"PKIX-dibt","title":"pkix-path accepts 3 chains PKITS says are invalid: CRL revocation stopped firing","description":"## pkix-path accepts three chains NIST PKITS says are invalid

Found by running the diff harness locally against the committed baseline, after the CI gate had been red for over a week and I had wrongly called the drift benign twice.

  chain                                        baseline  now   ground truth
  4.15.4 Invalid delta-CRL Test4               fail      PASS  was correct -> now WRONG
  4.4.8 Invalid Unknown CRL Entry Ext Test8    fail      PASS  was correct -> now WRONG
  4.4.9 Invalid Unknown CRL Extension Test9    fail      PASS  was correct -> now WRONG

All three are PKITS chains whose names declare them Invalid, all three used to fail correctly, and all three now pass. ground_truth_agreement flipped True -> False on each. Total ground-truth disagreements went 46 -> 48.

Every baseline failure reason was the same shape:

  "pkix-path revocation: cert at chain index 0 revoked by CRL: certificate NN is revoked ..."

and the current reason is empty, because the chain passes. So CRL revocation checking used to fire on these chains and no longer does. A revoked certificate is being accepted.

## This is the severe direction

LooserThanWild is rank 0 of 5 in this harness for a reason: accepting what others reject is how a validator gets someone compromised. pkix-path is published at 0.4.0 on crates.io, so this is not theoretical.

## One genuine fix in the same set

4.15.7 Valid delta-CRL Test7 went the other way: ground_truth_agreement False -> True. pkix-path used to wrongly reject a valid chain (reason removeFromCRL) and now accepts it correctly. So whatever changed is not purely a loss -- it looks like a change in delta-CRL / CRL-entry-extension handling that fixed one case and broke three.

That shape -- one fix, three regressions, all in CRL entry and delta-CRL handling -- is the strongest hint about where to look.

## Not the oracles

A separate and much larger drift IS oracle-side: pyca went pass -> fail on 20 chains, because cryptography 50.0.2 is far stricter than whatever version produced the baseline. That is real but benign, and it is what I mistook the whole picture for.

The four pkix-path flips are ours. Local reproduces CI exactly (63/58/93/33/0 across all five classes), and pkix-path is the same code in both, so the pkix-path half cannot be explained by the runner.

## Where to look

- The baseline was generated before 2026-11-16, when diff-harness first went red. The regression landed on or before that date and predates this session's 61 commits.
- All four chains are CRL-related: delta-CRL indicator handling, unknown CRL entry extensions, unknown CRL extensions.
- 4.4.8 and 4.4.9 are specifically about UNKNOWN extensions on a CRL or a CRL entry. RFC 5280 section 5.2 requires an unrecognized CRITICAL CRL extension to make the CRL unusable, and section 5.3 the same for a critical CRL entry extension. If a recent change started ignoring unknown critical CRL extensions instead of rejecting them, these three chains are exactly what would break -- and 4.15.7, which hinges on removeFromCRL in a delta CRL, is exactly what would be fixed.
  That is a hypothesis from the chain names and the reason strings, NOT a diagnosis. Confirm it before changing code.
- `git log --oneline -- pkix-revocation/src pkix-path/src` around and before 2026-11-16 is the place to start. A bisect over the four chains would settle it.

## Do not regenerate the baseline

The obvious wrong move is `cp fresh baseline` to make CI green. Three of these are NIST saying a chain must be rejected and pkix-path accepting it. The baseline is right and the code is wrong.

[ ] Identify the commit that changed CRL entry / delta-CRL handling, by bisect over these four chains
[ ] Decide per chain whether the new behaviour is defensible against RFC 5280 sections 5.2 and 5.3, or a bug to revert

{"notes":"RE-AIMED 2026-11-25. My P0 framing pointed at the wrong component. The library change is CORRECT; the diff harness's oracle adapter is what fails open. Downgraded P0 -> P2.

## What the local run established

Local reproduces CI exactly: 63/58/93/33/0 across all five classes, total 247. Since pkix-path is the same code in both, the pkix-path half cannot be a runner artifact.

24 chains changed class. Per-oracle verdict flips:

  pyca       pass -> fail   20 chains   (cryptography 50.0.2 vs the baseline's older version)
  pkix-path  fail -> pass    4 chains

The pyca half is a genuine oracle version effect and benign.

The four pkix-path flips, against PKITS ground truth:

  4.15.4 Invalid delta-CRL Test4             fail -> pass   gt True  -> False
  4.4.8  Invalid Unknown CRL Entry Ext Test8 fail -> pass   gt True  -> False
  4.4.9  Invalid Unknown CRL Extension Test9 fail -> pass   gt True  -> False
  4.15.7 Valid delta-CRL Test7               fail -> pass   gt False -> True   (a fix)

## The cause, and why the library is not at fault

Commit a407f615 "fix(pkix-revocation): stop CRL checks reporting not-revoked when they cannot tell" made a CRL whose own or whose entries' extensions carry an unrecognized critical extension UNUSABLE, returning Error::CrlUnsupportedCriticalExtension. That is RFC 5280 sections 5.2 and 5.3, and its own message cites fixing PKITS 4.4.10 -- the direct sibling of the regressed 4.4.8 and 4.4.9.

That change is right. What fails open is the harness's oracle adapter, which documents its policy in its own source:

  "Only the Revoked case flips the verdict. Every other outcome -- including
   Ok (CRL applied, cert not on list) and Err (CRL did not apply: mismatch /
   scope / parse / signature failure) -- is treated as 'this CRL has no
   negative determination, try the next'."

So before a407f615 these CRLs were applied, reported Revoked, and the chain failed. After it they are correctly rejected as unusable, the adapter ignores the error, no other CRL applies, and the chain passes.

The library delegates this policy deliberately and says so: "Callers enforcing a hard-fail revocation policy should treat OutOfScope [as a failure]." The harness is a soft-fail caller by design, which was defensible when an unusable CRL meant a mismatch and is not once it can mean "this CRL must not be used at all".

## So the defect is in the oracle adapter

It no longer models a PKITS-conformant validator for chains whose only CRL is unusable. PKITS classes those chains invalid precisely because a validator that cannot determine revocation status must fail closed. The adapter needs to distinguish:

- "CRL applied, certificate not listed"  -> no determination, try the next CRL
- "no CRL could be applied at all"       -> undetermined, and for PKITS that means FAIL

## What I did NOT verify, and it is the one thing that matters for consumers

Whether pkix-path's own Verifier fails open the same way. I traced the harness adapter and a pkix-chain wrapper, not the main validator call site. If the real validation path also ignores a CrlUnsupportedCriticalExtension and proceeds, then a hard-fail consumer is affected and this goes back up in priority.

Do that check first. It is a few minutes of reading and it decides whether this is a harness-only issue.

## Corrections to my earlier claims, all in this bead's history

- "pkix-path accepts three chains PKITS says are invalid" -- true of the HARNESS result, misleading about where the defect is.
- "CRL revocation stopped firing" -- wrong. Revocation checking is working better; the CRLs are being correctly refused.
- "a revoked certificate is being accepted" -- overstated. A certificate whose revocation status cannot be determined from a usable CRL is being accepted by a soft-fail oracle.

## Acceptance

[ ] Determine whether pkix-path's own Verifier fails open on an unusable CRL; if it does, re-raise and fix that first
[ ] Harness adapter distinguishes "no usable CRL" from "CRL applied, not revoked", and fails closed for the former
[ ] Re-run and confirm 4.15.4, 4.4.8, 4.4.9 return to failing and 4.15.7 stays fixed
[ ] Baseline regenerated afterwards, covering the pyca 50.x drift and the 4.15.7 fix, with the reason recorded","priority":2,"title":"diff-harness oracle fails open on unusable CRLs; 3 PKITS invalid chains now pass"}

{"notes":"ADAPTER FIXED 2026-11-25. The fail-open is closed. Net ground-truth agreement improved by 10. Two of the three target chains fixed; 4.15.4 remains and has a different cause.

## The change

Per-CRL handling stays soft -- PKITS chains ship several CRLs of which only some apply, so an inapplicable CRL must not fail anything. What changed is per certificate:

  Ok(())                  -> a CRL reached a verdict; record it and keep going
  Err(Revoked)            -> revoked, fail (unchanged)
  Err(anything else)      -> this CRL carries no determination, try the next
  no CRL ever returned Ok -> status UNDETERMINED, fail closed  <-- new

This matches pkix_chain::verify_chain, which propagates every revocation error with `?` and has no soft-fail mode. The only difference is that the oracle holds a pool of CRLs and tries them all before concluding, where verify_chain holds one checker and fails on the first error.

Empty chain.crls is untouched: the caller skips this function entirely, preserving no-revocation behaviour for most of the corpus.

## Measured result against the committed baseline

  class                  baseline   before fix   after fix
  Agreement                    71           63          60
  DiagnosticDivergence         49           58          66
  LooserThanWild               81           93          44
  StricterThanWild             46           33          77
  OracleDivergence              0            0           0
  total                       247          247         247

  ground-truth disagreements   46           48          36

LooserThanWild more than halves, 93 -> 44. That is the fail-open closing.

Ground truth: 31 invalid chains now correctly rejected, 21 valid chains newly rejected, net 10 fewer disagreements with NIST.

Target chains:
  4.4.8  Invalid Unknown CRL Entry Extension Test8   FIXED, now fails, gt agrees
  4.4.9  Invalid Unknown CRL Extension Test9         FIXED, now fails, gt agrees
  4.15.7 Valid delta-CRL Test7                       still correctly passes
  4.15.4 Invalid delta-CRL Test4                     STILL PASSES, still wrong

## The 21 newly-failing valid chains are a surfaced gap, not a new bug

Twenty of them fail with the new undetermined reason. By PKITS section: nine in 4.14, three in 4.5, two each in 4.6 and 4.12, one each in 4.4, 4.9, 4.11, 4.13, 4.15.

Section 4.14 is distribution points -- exactly where pkix-revocation returns OutOfScope for reason-partitioned and scope-restricted CRLs it cannot combine. a407f615 said so when it introduced that: "Combining reason-partitioned CRLs is not implemented, so valid vectors such as PKITS 4.14.18 are now out of scope rather than passed."

So these chains fail because pkix-revocation genuinely cannot determine their revocation status, and a hard-fail validator must then reject. PKITS classes them valid because a complete implementation would combine the CRLs. The oracle now reports that limitation instead of papering over it, which is what a differential harness is for.

Whether to implement reason-partitioned CRL combining is a separate question and probably its own bead. It is a real missing feature with 20 PKITS vectors behind it.

## 4.15.4 is still wrong, and the baseline must not be regenerated yet

4.15.4 Invalid delta-CRL Test4 still passes. Some CRL applies to it cleanly, so cleared_by_some_crl is set and the undetermined path is never reached. Its cause is different from the other two and is not yet understood.

Regenerating the baseline now would bless a chain NIST says must be rejected. Do not do it until 4.15.4 is explained.

## Remaining acceptance

[x] Determined pkix-path's own Verifier fails closed -- it does, with a bare `?` and no soft-fail mode
[x] Harness adapter distinguishes "no usable CRL" from "CRL applied, not revoked" and fails closed for the former
[x] 4.4.8 and 4.4.9 return to failing; 4.15.7 stays fixed
[ ] Explain why 4.15.4 still passes -- a CRL applies to it cleanly, so the delta/base interaction is the place to look
[ ] Decide on reason-partitioned CRL combining, which 20 of the 21 newly-failing valid chains depend on
[ ] Only then regenerate the baseline, recording the pyca 50.x drift, the 4.15.7 fix, and the newly-surfaced gap"}

## Why 4.15.4 still passed after the fail-closed fix

The oracle built one CrlChecker::new per CRL and never called with_delta. A delta CRL is only meaningful alongside its base, so handed one alone pkix-revocation correctly refuses it as DeltaCrlAsComplete. Delta CRLs were therefore unusable by construction, and a certificate revoked ONLY in a delta was never seen as revoked -- the base cleared it, the delta was refused, and the fail-closed path never fired because the base legitimately returned Ok.

Probed with the actual PKITS fixtures, EE cert InvaliddeltaCRLTest4EE against the three CRLs the vector ships:

  deltaCRLCA1CRL      (base)  -> Ok(())
  deltaCRLCA1deltaCRL (delta) -> Err(DeltaCrlAsComplete)
  base + delta via with_delta -> Err(Revoked { serial 3, reason KeyCompromise })

## The uncomfortable part, worth keeping

The committed baseline records 4.15.4 as correctly failing. It got that right for the WRONG reason: before a407f615, a standalone delta was accepted as a complete CRL, found serial 3 revoked, and failed the chain. That acceptance is precisely the hole a407f615 closed -- an on-path attacker could serve the CA's own validly signed delta at a plain-http CDP URL and un-revoke anything listed only in the base.

So three layers were involved and only the middle one was ever right:

  pkix-revocation   correct -- refuses a standalone delta, pairs properly via with_delta
  harness adapter   wrong   -- fed CRLs singly, so deltas could never be used
  committed baseline right answer, wrong reason -- recorded the pre-fix delta-as-complete behaviour

A baseline can encode a vulnerability as an expectation. That is worth remembering the next time one looks authoritative.

Every (base, delta) combination is offered to with_delta, which enforces the real rules itself: the base must not be a delta (§5.2.4), the delta's IssuingDistributionPoint must match the base's (§6.3.3(c)), CRL numbers must be consistent. A pairing that does not belong fails to construct and is dropped. Keeping the matching rules in the library rather than restating them in the harness is deliberate.

Each base is also kept unpaired, since a certificate revoked in the base must still be caught when no delta applies. Standalone deltas are not added -- they can only return DeltaCrlAsComplete.
